summary.title: Know your unknowns
summary.one_liner: A gallery of eleven self-contained HTML artifacts, each paired with the prompt that generated it, showing how to use Claude to surface unknowns before, during, and after implementation.
takeaways: Ask for a blindspot pass on unfamiliar code to list unknown unknowns with copyable prompt fixes.
Use Claude to interview you one question at a time about ambiguous features, ordered by architectural impact, then produce a decisions table.
Mock, prototype, or compare design directions before touching real code to find unknowns cheaply.
Have Claude keep a log of deviations from the plan during implementation so future attempts go better.
Before merging, use a pitch doc to pre-answer reviewer objections and a quiz to confirm you understand the change.
summary.summary: This companion page to a blog post presents eleven standalone HTML artifacts for finding unknowns at different stages of work. Each demo shows the exact prompt at the top and the artifact Claude produced below it, so readers can paste a prompt and get a similar result. Demos are grouped into pre-implementation (eight demos such as blindspot passes, mocks, interviews, and tweakable plans), during implementation (one deviation log), and post-implementation (a buy-in pitch doc and a merge-readiness quiz). The page is an example gallery rather than a detailed written tutorial.
